chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Ubayd, from Yunus, from one of his companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'While Musa (peace be upon him) was seated, Iblees came towards him, and upon him was a hood with various colors. So when he approached Musa (peace be upon him), he removed the hood and stood by Musa and greeted him. So Musa (peace be upon him) said to him: "Who are you?" He said: "I am Iblees." Musa said: "You, may Allah bring close your dwelling." He said: "Indeed, I only came to greet you due to your status with Allah."'

He (peace be upon him) said: 'So Musa (peace be upon him) said to him: "So what is this hood?" He said: "By it I snatch the hearts of the children of Adam." Musa said: "So inform me of the sin which, when the son of Adam commits it, you gain mastery over him." He said: "When his self astounds him, and he considers his deeds numerous, and his sin seems small in his eyes."'

And he (peace be upon him) said: 'Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said to Dawood (peace be upon him): "O Dawood! Give glad tidings to the sinners and warn the truthful." He said: "How do I give glad tidings to the sinners and warn the truthful?" He said: "O Dawood! Give glad tidings to the sinners that I accept repentance and pardon the sin, and warn the truthful that they should not be self-conceited with their deeds, for there is no servant whom I set up for reckoning except that he would be destroyed."'
ai.seo_question: What is the specific sin that allows Satan to gain mastery over a person according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* elucidates the subtle mechanism of *istikbar* (self-conceit) as Iblees' primary tool for deviation, linking it directly to the spiritual danger of overestimating one's righteous deeds. It complements the divine instruction to Prophet Dawood (AS) by distinguishing between the mercy extended to sinners who repent and the cautionary warning for the *siddiqun* (truthful ones), whose self-satisfaction can lead to their destruction despite their piety.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from Muhammad Bin Isa Bin Ubeyd, from Yunus, from one of his companions, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘While Musa<sup>as</sup> was seated, Iblees<sup>la</sup> came over and upon him<sup>la</sup> was a colourful hood.

So when he<sup>la</sup> approached Musa<sup>as</sup>, removed the hood and stood by him<sup>as</sup> and greeted upon him<sup>as</sup>. So Musa<sup>as</sup> said to him<sup>la</sup>: ‘Who are you<sup>la</sup>?’ So he<sup>la</sup> said, ‘I<sup>la</sup> am Iblees<sup>la</sup>’. He<sup>as</sup> said: ‘You<sup>la</sup>, May Allah<sup>azwj</sup> not let your<sup>la</sup> circling be close by’. He<sup>la</sup> said, ‘But rather, I<sup>la</sup> came over to greet upon you<sup>as</sup> due to your<sup>as</sup> status from Allah<sup>azwj</sup>’.

He<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> said: ‘So Musa<sup style="font-weight: normal">as</sup> said to him: ‘So what is this hood?’ He<sup style="font-weight: normal">la</sup> said, ‘By it I<sup style="font-weight: normal">la</sup> abduct the hearts of the children of Adam<sup style="font-weight: normal">as</sup>’. So Musa<sup style="font-weight: normal">as</sup> said: ‘So tell me<sup style="font-weight: normal">as</sup> of the sin which, when the son of Adam<sup style="font-weight: normal">as</sup> commits it, he gets captured upon it’. He<sup style="font-weight: normal">la</sup> said, ‘When his self astounds him and his deeds seem numerous and his sins seem small in his eyes’.

And he<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> said: ‘Allah<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic Said to Dawood<sup style="font-weight: normal">as</sup>: “O Dawood<sup style="font-weight: normal">as</sup>! Give glad tidings to the sinners and warn the truthful!” He<sup style="font-weight: normal">as</sup> said: ‘How do I<sup style="font-weight: normal">as</sup> give glad tidings to the sinners and warn the truthful?’ He<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> Said: “O Dawood<sup style="font-weight: normal">as</sup>! Give glad tidings to the sinners that I<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> Accept the repentance and Pardon the sins, and warn the truthful that they should not be self-conceited with their deeds, for there is no servant who will be linked with it for the Reckoning except that he would be destroyed!”’.
en.sarwar: 8. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from Muhammad ibn ‘Isa ibn ‘Ubayd from Yunus from certain individuals of his people from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following:

“The Messenger of Allah has said, ‘Once Moses was sitting when Satan came to him with a many-colored hooded cloak on him. When he approached Moses he took his cloak off, stood nearby, and offered him the greeting of peace. Moses asked, ‘Who are you?’ He replied, ‘I am Satan.’ Moses said, ‘Is it you? May Allah not bring you near by.’ Satan said, ‘I came to offer you greetings of peace because of your closeness to Allah.’

The Imam said, ‘Moses then asked, ‘What is this hooded cloak for?’ He said, ‘With this I kidnap the hearts of the children of Adam.’ Moses said, ‘Tell me which sin is it that when the children of Adam commit it you feel successful?’ He said, ‘It is when he feels self-important, his good deeds are a great deal and his sins trivial. ’

“The Imam said, ‘Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Holy, said to David, “O David, give good news to the sinners and warn the true believers.” He asked, ‘How should I give good news to the sinners and warn the true believers?’ Allah said, ‘Give good news to the sinners that I accept repentance and forgive their sins. Warn the true believers against feeling self-important due to their deeds. If I will ever make anyone settle his accounts, he is destroyed.’”
